newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch probe EU summit assassination poster threat.
newsitem.headline: Dutch probe EU summit assassination poster threat.

text.p: Police said on Friday they were investigating an outbreak of posters in Amsterdam calling for the assassination of European leaders at next week's EU summit.
"The people responsible will be arrested and charged with incitement," spokesman Klaas Wilting said. "There are all kinds of protests on the go...but this is taking things too far."

The posters, depicting the head-and-shoulder portraits of European leaders including Britain's Tony Blair, Germany's Helmut Kohl and France's Jacques Chirac in star-shaped targets, urge passers-by to "search and destroy".
"Take your chance and make history of them," the English-language poster urges, adding "These targets will be moved around. An army of 10,000 cops cannot protect them. Let's bring them down."
Activists are told to use their fists, stones, paint and smoke-bombs and molotov cocktails.

The posters bear all the hallmarks of Amsterdam's radical -- but usually harmless -- squatter movement, which has wound down since its violent 1980s heyday as many of its punk supporters have grown older and succumbed to yuppiedom or become parents.
Wilting said police saw no reason to further escalate the high levels of security at the summit, to be held at the Dutch central bank in Amsterdam's city centre on June 16 and 17.
"We have 5,000 police on the alert, we need not step up security further," he said, adding that police were taking the incident "very seriously".
